subject: guys named Steve
one_liner: Frontend infrastructure for developers named Steve, resolved by middle initial.
brand_voice_notes: Straight-faced platform company. Talks in p50s, region counts and resolver latency about a problem that is entirely nominal. Publishes an identity manual before it publishes documentation. Never once acknowledges that the constraint is a first name, and treats every Steve as a routing decision rather than a person.

hero.h1: Every deploy lands on a Steve.
hero.sub: Stevedore is the frontend platform for engineering organisations that are structurally unable to tell their Steves apart. Push to main, and the resolver decides which one of you did it. 41 regions. 41,208 verified Steves. Disambiguation at the edge, in under 400ms.

features.title: Named-origin routing
features.blurb: Every deployment resolves to a hostname derived from your legal first name, so all of them are the same hostname. When two Steves push to one project, production traffic splits by middle initial. Steves without a middle initial are round-robined until one of them files a ticket.

features.title: The disambiguation index
features.blurb: We maintain a global registry of every verified Steve and assign each one a stable numeric suffix at signup. The suffix is permanent, non-transferable, and load-bearing across your entire build pipeline. It is not shown to you.

features.title: Rollback to a previous Steve
features.blurb: Builds are immutable and attributed. When production breaks, roll back to the last Steve who did not break it. He is notified at the time of rollback, at his registered address, whether or not he still works here.

pricing_tiers.name: Steve
pricing_tiers.tagline: One name, one project, no guarantees about which of you gets it.
perks: Suffix reassigned on the first of each month

pricing_tiers.name: Steve Pro
pricing_tiers.tagline: For Steves who have been asked to stop pushing on Fridays.
perks: Middle initial stored in a durable region

pricing_tiers.name: Steven
pricing_tiers.tagline: For organisations with more than nine Steves and no plan for that.
perks: Custom split weights per middle initial

testimonials.quote: We had four Steves and one repository. We now have four Steves, one repository, and a numbering system that none of us agreed to and none of us can see.
testimonials.name: Steve Kowalczyk
testimonials.title: Staff Engineer, Platform Identity, Halcyon Freight Systems

testimonials.quote: The rollback notified the wrong Steve for six weeks. Support explained, patiently, that this is the notification working.
testimonials.name: Steve O Ruairc
testimonials.title: Director of Release Engineering, Merriwether Dental Group

testimonials.quote: I am Steve 00417. I have never been shown that number. I learned it from a colleague's error log and I think about it most evenings.

testimonials.title: Interim VP of Frontend, Coastal Ledger Systems

demo_screen_concept: The Stevedore resolver console for the project 'marketing-site', where every commit author is Steve. A left rail lists the organisation's verified Steves with their numeric suffixes, middle initials, current routing weight, and a status chip (RESOLVED, AMBIGUOUS, CONTESTED). The main panel is a deployments table where each row shows the commit message, the Steve the resolver picked, its confidence, and a build state; clicking a row opens a drawer that shows the resolution trace step by step (middle initial matched, timestamp compared, coin flipped) and offers a Promote to production button that flips the row's state live. Filter chips narrow by build state, a search field filters the Steve rail, a tab bar switches between Deployments, Steves and Routing, and the Routing tab shows middle-initial split weights as adjustable bars that must total 100%.

images.rationale: Hero skipped because the design direction is supergraphic identity-manual typography, where the hero is a CSS-built quarter-circle arc plate and a photograph would fight the flat flood. Demo subject assets skipped because demo_screen_concept is a resolver console (table, rail, drawer, split-weight bars), which is not photo-shaped. Full budget went to three testimonial headshots: 1974 corporate annual-report portraits of Steves, which is exactly the artefact a brand standards manual would reproduce, shot on the page palette so they sit inside the bands. Three of four slots used, all accepted on the first attempt.

items.prompt: Editorial corporate annual-report portrait photograph, 1974. A single middle-aged white man with a thick moustache and side-parted brown hair, wearing a wide-lapel brown suit and a knitted tie, seated at a three-quarter angle, looking directly into the lens with a flat neutral unsmiling expression. Warm faded film grain, soft even studio key light, shallow depth of field. Plain muted manual-stock cream backdrop #F6EDDC with a single flat deep teal #0E5C55 colour band running horizontally behind his shoulder. One focal subject only, centred, square composition. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens.
items.verdict: accepted: correct subject and period, teal band reads as the page motif, deadpan expression, no text artifacts

design_direction.style: Supergraphic corporate identity manual, 1974, manual-stock daylight mode. The page is staged as the issued brand standards document of a heavily funded frontend platform company that has decided a first name is a routing primitive and files your colleague under namespace collision. A warm manual-stock cream ground (#F6EDDC) runs the whole page with no gradients, no glass, no blur, no clay volume, no bento lattice, no photographic press plates and no drawing-sheet chrome: every division is a 1px ink hairline, a flat flood of one of two colours, or a hard-edged geometric shape, corners are 0px on plates and fully round on marks, and every shadow is banned. The organizing move is the band: full-bleed horizontal colour bands, each opened by a giant quarter-circle arc built in pure CSS border-radius, so sections arrive as supergraphic plates in a standards manual rather than as cards on a website. The core motif is the roundel: a concentric teal ring with a knocked-out capital S, used as the Steve identity mark, the list bullet, the pricing tier badge, the testimonial portrait frame and the section marker, always rotating a quarter turn on hover, so every element on the page is stamped as an approved use of the mark. The second motif is the clause number: every section is numbered as a manual clause (3.1 CORRECT USE OF THE STEVE) with a wide-tracked mono caption and a PLATE number, so the reader is turning pages of usage rules issued to Steves rather than reading marketing. One identity teal (#0E5C55) is the sole carrier: the wordmark, every band, every primary CTA, the roundels, and one word per headline, always as a flat flood with cream knocked out of it. One rationed oxblood (#8E2434) is quarantined strictly to identity telemetry (contested Steves, ambiguous resolutions, unresolved middle initials, suffix reassignment warnings, the coin-flip line in the resolution trace) and appears nowhere decorative, so the only second colour on the page is always the resolver admitting it does not know which Steve this is. Jost sets the wordmark and headlines in wide geometric grotesque caps at monumental sizes with identity-manual authority, tracking tightened to -0.02em at display sizes. Newsreader carries plain, faintly annual-report body copy at 17px with a 1.62 line-height. Every figure that pretends to be resolver telemetry (suffix numbers, confidence scores, split weights, region counts, p50 latencies, tier prices) is set in Space Mono with tabular figures inside hairline-ruled cream wells, so it reads like the index, not marketing. Motion is manual-restrained: bands wipe in from the left once on reveal, arcs sweep their quarter turn on load, roundels rotate 90 degrees on hover, CTAs invert to a teal flood on hover and depress 1px on press, split-weight bars fill once on scroll, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No dark mode, no glass, no blur, no gradients, no clay shadow pairs, no offset sticker shadows, no bento lattice, no hatch fills, no drawing-sheet title blocks, no didone engraving, no split-flap numerals, no mirrored type, no HUD brackets, no engraved seals, no catalog stitching, no emoji. Reads like a company that files your first name under 'origin' and considers your middle initial the only interesting thing about you.
design_direction.archetype: Developer-infrastructure platform product page issued as a corporate identity manual: banded hero with a monumental geometric claim over a CSS-built arc plate and a resolver telemetry strip, three numbered feature clauses on alternating cream and teal bands, testimonial plates with roundel-framed portraits and Steve suffixes, three pricing tiers laid out as a licensing schedule with roundel badges, closing CTA band, handoff to the resolver console demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Bands wipe left to right on reveal (420ms, ease-out). Quarter-circle arcs sweep once on load. Roundels rotate 90 degrees on hover (240ms). CTAs invert to teal flood on hover, depress 1px on press. Split-weight bars fill left to right once on scroll. Sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger. All motion gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Full-bleed cream plate opened by a giant teal quarter-circle arc anchored bottom-left, with the clause number 1.0 and a wide-tracked mono caption above a monumental Jost caps headline set to three lines, one word flooded teal. The roundel sits at the top-right of the plate at 96px. Beneath the headline, a hairline-ruled telemetry strip in Space Mono carries verified Steves, regions, resolver p50 and contested count, with the contested figure in oxblood. Primary CTA is a hard-edged teal flood, secondary is a hairline outline linking to the demo.
